definitions.explanation: Objects used on stage or in film to support the performance. Includes items that actors handle or interact with during a scene.
Small handy tools or accessories used for a specific purpose.

examples.japanese: {舞台|ぶたい}の{小道具|こどうぐ}を{準備|じゅんび}する。
examples.english: Prepare the props for the stage.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}では{小道具|こどうぐ}の{一|ひと}つ{一|ひと}つにこだわっている。
examples.english: In this film, great care is taken with each and every prop.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{小道具|こどうぐ}{担当|たんとう}として{長年|ながねん}{劇団|げきだん}を{支|ささ}えてきた。
examples.english: She has supported the theater company for many years as the props manager.

examples.japanese: {裁縫|さいほう}の{小道具|こどうぐ}をそろえる。
{台所|だいどころ}の{小道具|こどうぐ}が{増|ふ}えてきた。
examples.english: The small kitchen gadgets have been piling up.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}に{便利|べんり}な{小道具|こどうぐ}を{百円|ひゃくえん}ショップで{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought handy little travel accessories at a hundred-yen shop.

notes:
USAGE:
The theatrical sense (sense 1) is the most common usage. In stage and film production, {小道具|こどうぐ} refers to hand props and smaller set items, as opposed to {大道具|おおどうぐ} (large set pieces like furniture, walls, and backdrops).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小道具|こどうぐ}{担当|たんとう}: props manager
- {小道具|こどうぐ}{係|がかり}: person in charge of props
- {小道具|こどうぐ}を{用意|ようい}する: to prepare props
